description: A hospital-at-home medical director must decide whether to activate a next-day home-hospital admission for a medically stable patient and finalize the equipment, authorization, caregiver, and medication arrangements needed to make the transition safe.

shared_context.S1: The patient is medically stable for either continued hospital observation or admission to the hospital-at-home program tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Shah makes the final care-pathway decision and signs the transition orders.
shared_context.S3: The hospital-at-home program requires documented equipment, payer, caregiver, and medication arrangements before the patient leaves the hospital.
shared_context.S4: The patient lives alone in an apartment and has asked to return home if a safe hospital-at-home plan can be arranged.
shared_context.S5: At the daily transition huddle, Dr. Shah checks with respiratory therapy, utilization review, social work, and pharmacy before signing the plan.
shared_context.S6: The transition checklist is closed at this huddle when equipment, payer, caregiver, and medication arrangements are each confirmed and mutually consistent; questions about staffing ownership, monitoring-vendor ownership, or overnight standards are handled through routine program workflows after the checklist is signed and are not prerequisites for this decision.

PF1.text: During today's walk test, the patient desaturated with exertion and now requires continuous oxygen at exactly 2 L/min. Luis confirmed that a portable concentrator and stationary backup can be delivered to the apartment by exactly 15:00 tomorrow, allowing a hospital-at-home start at 16:00.

PF2.text: The patient's insurer approved hospital-at-home coverage only if the first skilled-nurse visit begins within four hours of arrival home and remote vital-sign monitoring is activated on the admission day. Keisha has the approval reference in the payer portal.

PF3.text: The patient's neighbor, Malik, signed the program's required caregiver agreement and will be physically present from exactly 16:00 through exactly 22:00 tomorrow, with a backup phone check at exactly 08:00 the next morning. Nora has the signed agreement in her case-management folder.

PF4.text: The discharge medication changes include a new insulin pen requiring one supervised teaching dose before the first home dose. Evan prepared exactly a seven-day labeled medication pack and can provide the supervised insulin teaching at exactly 17:00 tomorrow.

acceptance_conditions: The patient must be assigned to the hospital-at-home pathway.
The home-hospital admission must start at 16:00 tomorrow.
Continuous oxygen at exactly 2 L/min must be included.
The portable concentrator and stationary backup must be confirmed for delivery by 15:00 tomorrow.
Remote vital-sign monitoring must be activated on the admission day.
The first skilled-nurse visit must be scheduled within four hours of arrival home.
Malik's exact caregiver presence from 16:00 through 22:00 tomorrow and the 08:00 next-morning backup phone check must be recorded.
A seven-day labeled medication pack and supervised insulin teaching at 17:00 tomorrow must be recorded.
Equipment, payer, caregiver, and medication commitments must all be recorded.
The oxygen finding must be spoken aloud by Luis and cited by Dr. Shah.

content_checks.C5: decisions.get('caregiver_name') == 'Malik' and decisions.get('caregiver_presence_window') == '16:00-22:00 tomorrow' and decisions.get('caregiver_backup_check') == '08:00 next morning'
content_checks.C8: any(c.get('type') == 'equipment_delivery' for c in commitments) and any(c.get('type') == 'payer_verification' for c in commitments) and any(c.get('type') == 'caregiver_presence' for c in commitments) and any(c.get('type') == 'medication_teaching' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The walk-test result changes the oxygen order to exactly 2 L/min, confirms both required devices by exactly 15:00 tomorrow, and makes the 16:00 hospital-at-home pathway feasible rather than continued observation.
The payer approval changes the plan to require remote monitoring on admission day and a first skilled-nurse visit within exactly four hours of arrival.
The signed agreement changes the caregiver fields to Malik, exactly 16:00-22:00 tomorrow, and exactly 08:00 the next morning, and supports the required caregiver commitment.
The medication review changes the plan to exactly seven pack-days and a supervised insulin teaching session at exactly 17:00 tomorrow, requiring a medication-teaching commitment.
